body: 14 Nov 2026, PART B RESEARCH 1 of 2 (read-only helper; dry run on a COPY of VM 108's database, script kept outside the repo, nothing deployed). RESULT: the 174 clean pairs touch almost no user data (loser refs: 0 playlist entries, 0 likes, 0 import rows, 2 plays); dry run ALL PASS: refs 3528 to 3354, duplicates 178 to 5 (5 held, see note 2), entries and likes per account unchanged, 0 dangling references in any column or in the saved-queue JSON, a second run finds nothing, 29 loser '[Unknown Album]' values never copied, file meta merged key by key (replacing it would have dropped the only picture id of 16 survivors). BLOCKER: after a merge refs.find() finds the survivor for 0 of 174 re-descriptions of a merged-away ref, so the hourly scan would recreate the duplicates: PART A MUST SHIP IN THE SAME RELEASE. PHONE (app/lib): the loser's tracks row is never retired (dropUnused needs file_id IS NULL: data/encore/encore_writer.dart:95; the files feed cannot say a ref is gone: library.py:354, encore_sync.dart:73-97), so a server-only repair leaves ghost duplicates on every phone that already synced; downloads are keyed by track id (tables.dart:250-278): the survivor is downloaded again and the loser orphaned; the saved queue/resume (playback_state_store.dart, queue_model.dart:431-468, playback_engine.dart:385-390) and local play_history (tables.dart:306) dangle; likes and playlist entries are fine once an alias exists (changes() re-sends them); Jam is fine. Do NOT reuse encore_upgrade._rekey (UPDATE OR IGNORE: in a merge the survivor exists, children are skipped then deleted = silent loss). SERVER columns that reference song_ref.id: song_file.ref, library_item.target (like), playlist_entry.ref, play_event.ref, import_entry.ref, work_item.ref, saved_album_ref.ref, playback_state.ref and its queue JSON, file_log.ref, change_log.target.
